answer: Before a seafarer stands a watch, the flag state maritime administration checks the STCW certificate number against the discharge book and the sea service log, and a second identity reusing that number is refused at the manning office. A duplicate certificate or inflated sea time triggers suspension, a manning agent bond forfeit and a six month hiring freeze. Training runs 950 and the medical 180, while twelve months of sea time cannot be bought, so N fakes cost N x 1130 plus N years afloat. A signal flag on the bridge rail, a lotus on the funnel and a pigment stain change none of that.
